```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Article: Soeorg H, Lyu S, Kloprogge F, Standing JF. Pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic
  modeling using combined time-kill data for meropenem and colistin or polymyxin B
  combination effects in *Acinetobacter baumannii*. Antimicrob Agents Chemother. 2026.
  <https://doi.org/10.1128/aac.00274-26>
* Supplementary material (`aac.00274-26-s0001.docx`): the pooled studies
  (Table S1), the model-building steps (Table S2) and Figs. S1-S7. No erratum was
  listed on Europe PMC when the model was added (November 2026).

The authors pooled 369 published time-kill and hollow-fibre experiments and fitted
one model to all of them. Bacteria grow logistically and each drug kills through an
Emax term whose EC50 is a multiple of the isolate's MIC. Each drug's kill fades over
time through a two-state attenuation, and the two kills combine under Bliss
independence with a general pharmacodynamic interaction (GPDI): colistin/polymyxin B
raises the meropenem Emax and lowers its EC50. Colistin and polymyxin B share one
set of parameters.

```{r model}
mod <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Soeorg_2026_meropenem_colistin_polymyxinB"))
mod
```

The model has no dosing events. The drug concentrations, MICs, starting inoculum and
carbapenemase status are covariates on the observation rows, and a concentration can
vary over time when the model is driven from a PK profile:

| Covariate | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `CONC_MEROPENEM_MGL` | meropenem concentration (mg/L) |
| `CONC_COLISTIN_MGL`, `CONC_POLYMYXINB_MGL` | colistin and polymyxin B concentrations (mg/L); summed into one polymyxin concentration, so set the unused one to 0 |
| `MIC_MEROPENEM` | meropenem MIC of the isolate (mg/L) |
| `MIC_COLISTIN`, `MIC_POLYMYXINB` | colistin and polymyxin B MICs (mg/L); `MIC_POLYMYXINB` is used when `CONC_POLYMYXINB_MGL > 0`, otherwise `MIC_COLISTIN` |
| `CARBAPENEMASE_POS` | 1 = acquired carbapenemase (OXA-23, OXA-24/40, OXA-58, OXA-72, VIM-1, NDM-1) |
| `INOC_LOG10CFU` | starting inoculum (log10 CFU/mL) |

# Population (biological context)

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Soeorg_2026_meropenem_colistin_polymyxinB")()$population)
```

The data come from 21 papers (Table S1): 18 ran static time-kill experiments and 5
ran hollow-fibre infection models, mostly in cation-adjusted Mueller-Hinton broth at
35-37 degrees C. The 369 experiments covered 70 growth controls, 104 meropenem,
46 colistin, 37 polymyxin B, 53 meropenem + colistin and 59 meropenem + polymyxin B
arms against 53 strains (60 strain-paper "isolates"). Of the 60 isolates, 57 were
meropenem-resistant, 14 were colistin/polymyxin B-resistant and 30 carried an
acquired carbapenemase (Fig. 1). Counts were digitised from the published figures,
and values below each study's limit of quantification were handled with the M3
method.

# Source trace

| Element | Value in the model | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Logistic growth with killing | `d/dt(cfu) <- (kg * (1 - cfu / 10^bmax) - kkill) * cfu` | Eq 1 |
| Initial count | `cfu(0) <- 10^INOC_LOG10CFU` | Eq 2 |
| Two-state attenuation, on only while drug is present | `aron_*`, `aroff_*` | Eq 3-6 |
| Meropenem Emax inoculum effect | `emax_mero * (INOC/6)^e_inoc_emax_mero` | Eq 7 |
| Colistin/polymyxin B Emax at 8 log10 inoculum | `emax_col * e_inoc8_emax_col^I(INOC = 8)` | Eq 8 |
| Meropenem kill | Emax x thetaBL x (1 + Int_Emax) x (1 - R_on) x C / (EC50 x MIC x (1 - Int_EC50) + C) | Eq 9 |
| Colistin/polymyxin B kill | Emax x (1 - R_on) x C / (EC50 x MIC + C) | Eq 10 |
| GPDI terms | Delta x C_COLPMB / (EC50_INTER x MIC_COLPMB + C_COLPMB) | Eq 11 |
| Bliss independence | `kkill = K_MERO + K_COLPMB - (K_MERO/Emax_MERO)(K_COLPMB/Emax_COLPMB) Eref`, `Eref = max(Emax)` | Eq 12-13 |
| `lkg` | 0.33 (Kgrowth = exp(0.33) = 1.39 1/h) | Table 1 Kgrowth 0.33, read as the log-scale estimate (see below) |
| `log10bmax` | 8.41 log10 CFU/mL | Table 1 Bmax |
| `etalog10bmax` | 0.11^2 | Table 1, Bmax IIV SD 0.11 |
| `emax_mero` | 3.47 1/h | Table 1 EmaxMERO |
| `kon_mero` | 0.033 1/h | Table 1 Katten,MERO |
| `e_inoc_emax_mero` | -0.63 | Table 1 gammaMERO |
| `e_carbapenemase_emax_mero` | 0.83 | Table 1 thetaBL |
| `lec50_mero` | log(1), fixed | Table 1 EC50MERO "Fixed to MIC" |
| `etalec50_mero` | 1.13^2 | Table 1, EC50MERO IIV SD 1.13 |
| `emax_col` | 3.62 1/h | Table 1 EmaxCOLPMB |
| `kon_col` | 0.075 1/h | Table 1 Katten,COLPMB |
| `e_inoc8_emax_col` | 0.005 | Table 1 gammaCOLPMB |
| `lec50_col` | log(0.33) | Table 1 EC50COLPMB (x MIC; linear in the MIC, Table S2 model P6) |
| `etalec50_col` | 1.35^2 | Table 1, EC50COLPMB IIV SD 1.35 |
| `int_emax_col_mero` | 0.29 | Table 1 Delta_Emax |
| `int_ec50_col_mero` | 1, fixed | Table 1 Delta_EC50 "1 (fix)" |
| `ec50int_col_mero` | 1 x MIC, fixed | **Not reported**; see Assumptions |
| `addSd` | 1.21 log10 CFU/mL | Table 1 residual SD 1.21 (additive on log10 CFU/mL; see Assumptions) |

```{r param-table}
  "e_carbapenemase_emax_mero",  0.83,  th[["e_carbapenemase_emax_mero"]],
  "EC50_MERO (x MIC)",          1,     exp(th[["lec50_mero"]]),
  "emax_col",                   3.62,  th[["emax_col"]],

  "e_inoc8_emax_col",           0.005, th[["e_inoc8_emax_col"]],
  "EC50_COLPMB (x MIC)",        0.33,  exp(th[["lec50_col"]]),
  "int_emax_col_mero",          0.29,  th[["int_emax_col_mero"]],
  "int_ec50_col_mero",          1,     th[["int_ec50_col_mero"]],
  "addSd",                      1.21,  th[["addSd"]],
  "IIV SD, Bmax",               0.11,  sqrt(om[["etalog10bmax"]]),
  "IIV SD, EC50_MERO",          1.13,  sqrt(om[["etalec50_mero"]]),
  "IIV SD, EC50_COLPMB",        1.35,  sqrt(om[["etalec50_col"]])
)
knitr::kable(paper, digits = 4)
# Every Table 1 value must be carried exactly.
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(paper$paper, unname(paper$file), tolerance = 1e-10)))
```

# Simulation helpers

```{r helpers}
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

# Typical-value solve over several isolates. rxode2 warns that a multi-subject
# simulation has no between-subject variability, which is the intent here.
solve_typ <- function(events, ...) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxSolve(mod_typ, events, ...),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("omega", conditionMessage(w))) invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  )
}

# One observation row per time per isolate, on the bacterial state; the
# covariates ride along on every row.
kill_events <- function(times, ...) {
  grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(...)
  grid$id <- seq_len(nrow(grid))
  defaults <- list(CONC_MEROPENEM_MGL = 0, CONC_COLISTIN_MGL = 0, CONC_POLYMYXINB_MGL = 0,
                   MIC_MEROPENEM = 16, MIC_COLISTIN = 1, MIC_POLYMYXINB = 1,
                   CARBAPENEMASE_POS = 0, INOC_LOG10CFU = 6)
  for (nm in setdiff(names(defaults), names(grid))) grid[[nm]] <- defaults[[nm]]
  tidyr::expand_grid(grid, time = times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0, cmt = "cfu") |>
    arrange(id, time) |>
    as.data.frame()
}
covs <- c("CONC_MEROPENEM_MGL", "CONC_COLISTIN_MGL", "CONC_POLYMYXINB_MGL", "MIC_MEROPENEM", "MIC_COLISTIN",
          "MIC_POLYMYXINB", "CARBAPENEMASE_POS", "INOC_LOG10CFU")
```

# Structural checks

## Growth control against the closed-form logistic solution

Without drug, Eq 1 is the logistic equation, whose solution is
`B(t) = Bmax / (1 + (Bmax / B0 - 1) exp(-kg t))`. Both sides use the same
parameters, so they must agree to solver precision.

```{r growth-closed-form}
ev_g <- kill_events(seq(0, 24, by = 1), INOC_LOG10CFU = c(4, 6, 8))
sim_g <- as.data.frame(solve_typ(ev_g, keep = covs))
kg <- exp(th[["lkg"]])
bmax <- 10^th[["log10bmax"]]
sim_g <- sim_g |>
  mutate(closed = log10(bmax / (1 + (bmax / 10^INOC_LOG10CFU - 1) * exp(-kg * time))))
stopifnot(max(abs(sim_g$log_cfu - sim_g$closed)) < 1e-4)
ggplot(sim_g, aes(time, log_cfu, colour = factor(INOC_LOG10CFU))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(aes(y = closed), shape = 1) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "log10 CFU/mL", colour = "Inoculum\n(log10 CFU/mL)",
       title = "Growth control: model (lines) vs closed-form logistic (circles)")
```

## Attenuation states

With the drug present from time zero, `R_on(t) = 1 - exp(-katten t)` for each drug.

```{r attenuation}
ev_a <- kill_events(c(0, 6, 12, 24), CONC_MEROPENEM_MGL = 16, CONC_COLISTIN_MGL = 1)
sim_a <- as.data.frame(solve_typ(ev_a))
stopifnot(
  max(abs(sim_a$aron_mero - (1 - exp(-th[["kon_mero"]] * sim_a$time)))) < 1e-6,
  max(abs(sim_a$aron_col - (1 - exp(-th[["kon_col"]] * sim_a$time)))) < 1e-6,
  max(abs(sim_a$aron_mero + sim_a$aroff_mero - 1)) < 1e-8
)
```

## Kill rates at time zero against Eq 7-13

At time zero both attenuation states are off, so the model's combined kill rate
`kkill` can be recomputed by hand from Table 1 and Eq 7-13. This checks the
inoculum, carbapenemase and interaction terms together.

```{r kill-hand}
ev_k <- kill_events(0,
  CONC_MEROPENEM_MGL = c(0, 4, 16, 64), CONC_COLISTIN_MGL = c(0, 0.25, 1),
  CARBAPENEMASE_POS = c(0, 1), INOC_LOG10CFU = c(5, 6, 8))
sim_k <- as.data.frame(solve_typ(ev_k, keep = covs))
hand <- with(sim_k, {
  emax_m <- 3.47 * (INOC_LOG10CFU / 6)^-0.63
  emax_c <- 3.62 * 0.005^(INOC_LOG10CFU >= 7.5)
  fint <- CONC_COLISTIN_MGL / (1 * MIC_COLISTIN + CONC_COLISTIN_MGL)
  k_m <- emax_m * 0.83^CARBAPENEMASE_POS * (1 + 0.29 * fint) * CONC_MEROPENEM_MGL /
    (1 * MIC_MEROPENEM * (1 - 1 * fint) + CONC_MEROPENEM_MGL)
  k_c <- emax_c * CONC_COLISTIN_MGL / (0.33 * MIC_COLISTIN + CONC_COLISTIN_MGL)
  k_m + k_c - (k_m / emax_m) * (k_c / emax_c) * pmax(emax_m, emax_c)
})
stopifnot(max(abs(sim_k$kkill - hand)) < 1e-8)

# Two readings of Table 1 the model must honour: meropenem alone at C = MIC gives
# half its Emax, and colistin alone at C = 0.33 x MIC gives half its Emax.
half <- as.data.frame(solve_typ(kill_events(0,
  CONC_MEROPENEM_MGL = c(0, 16), CONC_COLISTIN_MGL = c(0, 0.33)), keep = covs))
stopifnot(
  abs(half$kkill[half$CONC_MEROPENEM_MGL == 16 & half$CONC_COLISTIN_MGL == 0] - 3.47 / 2) < 1e-8,
  abs(half$kkill[half$CONC_MEROPENEM_MGL == 0 & half$CONC_COLISTIN_MGL == 0.33] - 3.62 / 2) < 1e-8
)
```

# Typical static time-kill curves

Typical-value curves for a strain with meropenem MIC 16 mg/L and colistin MIC
1 mg/L at a 6 log10 CFU/mL inoculum, the strain the paper uses for its clinical
simulations.

```{r static-curves, fig.height = 6}
regimens <- tribble(
  ~regimen,                         ~CONC_MEROPENEM_MGL, ~CONC_COLISTIN_MGL,
  "Control",                         0,             0,
  "Colistin 0.5 x MIC",              0,             0.5,
  "Meropenem 1 x MIC",              16,             0,
  "Colistin 0.5 x + meropenem 1 x MIC", 16,         0.5,
  "Colistin 0.5 x + meropenem 0.25 x MIC", 4,       0.5
)
ev_s <- tidyr::expand_grid(regimens, CARBAPENEMASE_POS = c(0, 1)) |>
  mutate(id = row_number()) |>
  tidyr::expand_grid(time = seq(0, 24, by = 0.25)) |>
  mutate(evid = 0, cmt = "cfu", CONC_POLYMYXINB_MGL = 0, MIC_MEROPENEM = 16, MIC_COLISTIN = 1,
         MIC_POLYMYXINB = 1, INOC_LOG10CFU = 6) |>
  as.data.frame()
sim_s <- as.data.frame(solve_typ(ev_s, keep = c("regimen", "CARBAPENEMASE_POS")))
ggplot(sim_s, aes(time, log_cfu, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~ ifelse(CARBAPENEMASE_POS == 1, "Acquired carbapenemase", "No acquired carbapenemase")) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = 2) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-2, 9)) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "log10 CFU/mL", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 2))
```

The combination kills faster than either drug alone, and the carbapenemase slows
the meropenem kill. Attenuation lets the bacteria regrow late in the experiment.

## Growth control against Figure 2

The pcVPC in Figure 2 shows the growth controls. Read off the figure by the
maintainers, the observed median at the 6 log10 CFU/mL inoculum rises from about
6.3 to about 8.3 log10 CFU/mL within 4 h. The model reproduces that rise.

```{r growth-fig2}
g <- as.data.frame(solve_typ(kill_events(c(0, 4), INOC_LOG10CFU = 6.3)))
g4 <- g$log_cfu[g$time == 4]
g4
# Kgrowth = 0.33 1/h as printed would give 6.86 log10 CFU/mL here; see Assumptions.
stopifnot(abs(g4 - 8.3) < 0.5)
```

# Clinical regimen: Figure 3 and the OVERCOME probabilities

The paper simulates the regimens of the OVERCOME trial: a colistin loading dose of
5 mg/kg colistin base activity (CBA) then 1.67 mg/kg every 8 h, alone or with
meropenem 1 g every 8 h. The patient is 67 years old, 60 kg, with serum creatinine
1.5 mg/dL, and the target is epithelial lining fluid. The model is driven by unbound
lung concentrations: colistin 44% unbound with 100% lung penetration, meropenem 62.5%
unbound with 25% lung penetration. The strain has colistin MIC 1 mg/L and meropenem
MIC 16 mg/L, and the inoculum is drawn from N(6, 0.25) log10 CFU/mL. The probability of
target attainment (PTA) is the fraction of isolates below 10 CFU/mL (1 log10) at
24 h, with interisolate and residual variability.

The paper took its PK from Garonzik et al. (2011, colistin) and Lan et al. (2022,
meropenem). Neither is in nlmixr2lib, so this vignette uses two packaged
critically-ill models as stand-ins: `Mohamed_2012_colistin` (CMS converting to
colistin) and `Zou_2026_meropenem` (clearance driven by creatinine clearance). Only
their typical profiles are used. The comparison is therefore approximate, especially
for meropenem.

```{r clinical-pk}
src_pk <- function(name) rxode2::zeroRe(rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb(name)))
t_grid <- seq(0, 24, by = 0.25)

# Colistin: 5 mg/kg CBA x 60 kg = 300 mg CBA = 720 mg CMS loading dose, then
# 100 mg CBA = 240 mg CMS every 8 h (2.4 mg CMS per mg CBA), 0.5-h infusions.
ev_cms <- rbind(
  data.frame(id = 1, time = c(0, 8, 16), amt = c(720, 240, 240),
             rate = c(1440, 480, 480), evid = 1, cmt = "central_cms", dvid = NA),
  data.frame(id = 1, time = t_grid, amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0, cmt = NA, dvid = 2)
)
pk_col <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(src_pk("Mohamed_2012_colistin"), ev_cms))

# Meropenem 1 g every 8 h as 0.5-h infusions; Cockcroft-Gault CrCL of the patient.
crcl <- (140 - 67) * 60 / (72 * 1.5)
ev_mem <- rxode2::et(amt = 1000, rate = 2000, cmt = "central", addl = 2, ii = 8) |>
  rxode2::et(t_grid, cmt = "central")
pk_mem <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(src_pk("Zou_2026_meropenem"), ev_mem,
                                params = c(CRCL = crcl)))

lung <- data.frame(time = t_grid,
                   colistin = pk_col$Cc_col * 0.44,
                   meropenem = pk_mem$Cc * 0.625 * 0.25)
lung |>
  pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "drug", values_to = "conc") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, conc)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~drug, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Unbound lung concentration (mg/L)",
       title = "Stand-in PK profiles driving the PD model")
```

```{r clinical-sim, fig.height = 5}
n_iso <- 200 # isolates per regimen and carbapenemase arm
set.seed(20261121)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261121)
arms <- tidyr::expand_grid(regimen = c("Colistin", "Combination"),
                           CARBAPENEMASE_POS = c(0, 1)) |>
  mutate(arm = row_number())
iso <- arms[rep(seq_len(nrow(arms)), each = n_iso), ] |>
  mutate(id = row_number(), INOC_LOG10CFU = rnorm(n(), 6, 0.25))
ev_c <- tidyr::expand_grid(iso, lung) |>
  mutate(CONC_MEROPENEM_MGL = ifelse(regimen == "Combination", meropenem, 0),
         CONC_COLISTIN_MGL = colistin, CONC_POLYMYXINB_MGL = 0,
         MIC_MEROPENEM = 16, MIC_COLISTIN = 1, MIC_POLYMYXINB = 1,
         evid = 0, cmt = "cfu") |>
  arrange(id, time) |>
  as.data.frame()
sim_c <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(mod, ev_c, keep = c("regimen", "CARBAPENEMASE_POS")))

# Figure 3 medians, read off the figure by the maintainers.
fig3 <- tribble(
  ~CARBAPENEMASE_POS, ~time, ~Colistin, ~Combination,
  0,  1, 6.23, 5.93,   0,  2, 6.10, 5.53,   0,  4, 5.66, 4.77,
  0,  8, 5.19, 3.84,   0, 12, 5.36, 3.05,   0, 16, 6.06, 3.18,
  0, 20, 6.80, 3.40,   0, 24, 7.32, 4.27,
  1,  1, 6.32, 6.01,   1,  2, 6.19, 5.71,   1,  4, 5.75, 4.97,
  1,  8, 5.36, 4.14,   1, 12, 5.53, 3.49,   1, 16, 6.19, 3.71,
  1, 20, 6.93, 4.03,   1, 24, 7.40, 5.10
) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Colistin, Combination), names_to = "regimen", values_to = "fig3")

bands <- sim_c |>
  group_by(regimen, CARBAPENEMASE_POS, time) |>
  summarise(med = median(ipredSim), lo = quantile(ipredSim, 0.1),
            hi = quantile(ipredSim, 0.9), .groups = "drop")
lab_bl <- function(x) ifelse(x == 1, "Acquired carbapenemase", "No acquired carbapenemase")
ggplot(bands, aes(time, med, colour = regimen, fill = regimen)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = fig3, aes(y = fig3), shape = 1, size = 2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ lab_bl(CARBAPENEMASE_POS)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-4, 9)) +
  labs(x = "Time after the start of treatment (h)", y = "log10 CFU/mL",
       colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
       title = "Simulated median and 80% interval (lines, bands) vs Figure 3 medians (circles)") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Replicates Figure 3 of Soeorg 2026 (with stand-in PK).

```{r clinical-pta}
pta <- sim_c |>
  filter(time == 24) |>
  group_by(regimen, CARBAPENEMASE_POS) |>
  summarise(PTA_model = 100 * mean(sim < 1), median24_model = median(ipredSim),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(PTA_paper = c(0, 0, 22.7, 9.3)[match(paste(regimen, CARBAPENEMASE_POS),
           c("Colistin 0", "Colistin 1", "Combination 0", "Combination 1"))]) |>
  left_join(filter(fig3, time == 24) |> select(-time), by = c("regimen", "CARBAPENEMASE_POS")) |>
  rename("Regimen" = regimen, "Carbapenemase" = CARBAPENEMASE_POS,
         "PTA, model (%)" = PTA_model, "PTA, paper (%)" = PTA_paper,
         "Median log10 CFU/mL at 24 h, model" = median24_model,
         "Median at 24 h, Figure 3" = fig3)
knitr::kable(pta, digits = 2)

col24 <- bands$med[bands$regimen == "Colistin" & bands$time == 24]
col_pta <- pta$`PTA, model (%)`[pta$Regimen == "Colistin"]
# Colistin alone depends only on the growth, colistin kill and attenuation
# parameters, and the stand-in colistin exposure is close to Garonzik's for
# this patient, so it is the cleanest check of the model against Figure 3:
# regrowth to about 7.3 log10 CFU/mL by 24 h and no target attainment.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(col24 - 7.35) < 1),
  all(col_pta < 5)
)
```

Colistin alone matches the paper: about 1 log10 of kill over the first 8 h, regrowth
to above 7 log10 CFU/mL by 24 h, and 0% target attainment. The combination gives a
higher PTA than the paper reports (22.7% without and 9.3% with an acquired
carbapenemase), and a smaller difference between the two carbapenemase arms. Two things in this
comparison are not from the paper. The meropenem stand-in PK and the 0.5-h infusion
are assumptions. The interaction potency EC50_INTER is not reported, and the
combination PTA is sensitive to it. The colistin-alone arm depends on neither.

# PKNCA

Not applicable. The model predicts bacterial counts in a time-kill system and has no
drug PK of its own; drug concentrations are inputs.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Kgrowth read as a log-scale estimate.** Table 1 prints Kgrowth = 0.33, and the
  model uses Kgrowth = exp(0.33) = 1.39 1/h. A net growth rate of 0.33 1/h cannot
  reproduce the paper's own simulations, whatever the colistin exposure. It gives
  a growth-control rise of only 0.56 log10 in 4 h, where Figure 2 shows about 2. It
  also gives about 80% colistin-alone target attainment for the OVERCOME regimen, where
  the paper reports 0%, and no regrowth by 24 h, where Figure 3 shows regrowth to 7.3
  log10 CFU/mL. With exp(0.33) all three agree. The maintainers read the printed 0.33
  as the NONMEM log-scale estimate, the usual way a rate constant is estimated. The
  authors have not confirmed this reading.
* **EC50_INTER not reported.** Eq 11 needs the colistin/polymyxin B potency of the
  interaction, EC50_INTER (a multiple of the polymyxin MIC). Table 1 gives no value,
  and the "Supplementary text" with the final equations, cited in the Table 1
  footnote, is not in the published supplement. The model fixes EC50_INTER to 1 x MIC.
  Methods models each EC50 as a x MIC^b with a and b "estimated or fixed to 1", and
  Table 1 likewise omits a value for EC50_MERO, which is fixed to the MIC. The
  authors have not confirmed this value.
* **Residual error.** Table 1 labels the residual error "proportional" with SD 1.21.
  The dependent variable is log10 CFU/mL (Figs 2 and S3), so the model treats the
  error as additive on the log10 scale, the usual meaning of "proportional" for
  log-transformed data. A 121% proportional error on the log10 count would be
  implausible.
* **Interisolate variability on Bmax.** The paper uses exponential IIV, and Table 1
  gives Bmax on the log10 scale (8.41), so the eta multiplies the log10 carrying
  capacity: `log10bmax * exp(eta)`.
* **Inoculum-8 indicator.** Eq 8 switches on at an inoculum of 8 log10 CFU/mL (the
  intended inocula were 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8). The model codes it as
  `INOC_LOG10CFU >= 7.5`.
* **Colistin and polymyxin B.** The paper pools them (Table S2 found no potency
  difference). The model sums the two concentration columns and takes the MIC of
  whichever drug is present.
* **Stand-in PK for Figure 3.** See the clinical section. The paper's colistin and
  meropenem PK models are not in nlmixr2lib. The colistin maintenance dosing is
  assumed to start 8 h after the loading dose, and all infusions to last 0.5 h.
* **Inoculum in the paper's simulations.** The N(6, 0.25) inoculum draw is a
  simulation choice, not part of the fitted model (no IIV on the inoculum was
  retained, Table S2).
* **Below-LOQ handling.** The fit used M3 censoring at each study's LOQ. The
  packaged model returns the uncensored log10 count.
